front: How do a high-water mark and a hurdle rate affect hedge fund incentive fees?
back: A high-water mark means incentive fees are paid only on gains above the fund's previous peak value. A hurdle rate must be exceeded first: a hard hurdle charges fees only above it, a soft hurdle charges on all gains once it is cleared.

front: European versus American distribution waterfall in private equity?
back: European (whole-of-fund): the GP earns carried interest only after LPs get back all contributed capital plus any preferred return. American (deal-by-deal): carry is paid per deal, so a clawback provision matters more.

front: How is a property valued with the direct capitalization method?
back: $\text{Value} = \frac{NOI_1}{\text{Cap rate}}$. A lower cap rate implies a higher value.

front: What are the components of a commodity futures return?
back: Spot price return + roll return + collateral (interest) return. Roll return is positive in backwardation and negative in contango.

front: Common trap: why do hedge fund index returns tend to look too good?
back: Survivorship bias (failed funds drop out) and backfill bias (funds add strong past histories when they join) both push reported index returns up.

front: Fund investing, co-investing and direct investing: how do they differ?
back: Fund investing: invest via a manager's fund (highest fees, least control). Co-investing: invest alongside the fund directly in a deal. Direct investing: buy assets without an intermediary (most control, needs most expertise).

front: What happens to measured risk in appraisal-based real estate indexes?
back: Appraisals smooth returns, so volatility and correlations with other assets are understated, making the asset class look more attractive in an optimizer.
